title: Muck
summary: MUCK, noun [Latin mucus.] 1. Dung in a moist state, or a mass of dung and putrefied vegetable matter. With fattening muck besmear the roots. 2. Something mean, vile or filthy. To run a muck to run mad

inlines.v: MUCK, noun [Latin mucus.] 1. Dung in a moist state, or a mass of dung and putrefied vegetable matter. With fattening muck besmear the roots. 2. Something mean, vile or filthy. To run a muck to run madly and attack all we meet. Running a muck is a phrase derived from the Malays, (in whose language amock signified to kill, ) applied to desperate persons who intoxicate themselves with opium and then arm themselves with a dagger and attempt to kill all they meet. MUCK, verb transitive To manure with muck
